post.title: Claude Messages
post.hook: iMessage for your Claude Code sessions, in one Node file with no dependencies.
post.summary: A local web app that lists every running Claude Code session as a chat thread, lets you message any of them, and can start new ones. It runs on plain Node 18 with no installs.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Claude Messages is an iMessage-style window onto every Claude Code session running on one machine. The sidebar lists sessions, each thread shows that session's conversation, and a compose button starts a new session. You start it with `node server.mjs` and open http://127.0.0.1:4417.

## Why
Several Claude Code sessions can run at once across the terminal and Claude Desktop. This gives them one place to read and reply, with typing dots and approval buttons.

## How it works
- **Discovery:** it reads `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, the record each live process keeps.
- **History:** it reads the tail of each session's transcript `.jsonl` (the last 1.5 MB) and then follows it.
- **Sending:** a session started here gets a user line on its stdin. Any other session gets one frame on its inbox socket, the same one `SendMessage` uses.
- **Approvals:** sessions started here run with `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`, so each request appears as a bubble with Allow and Deny.

The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only, rejects foreign Host or Origin headers, requires a token that changes each launch, and never reads session key files.

## Limits
- Messages to sessions started elsewhere arrive as from *another Claude session*, so they don't count as your approval.
- Bypass-mode sessions hold messages for approval in their own window.
- Replies come from the transcript, since the app has no reply address.
- Sessions started here stop when the server stops.
- macOS and Linux only.
- It relies on undocumented internals, checked against Claude Code 2.1.260 and 2.1.293.

## Open questions
The internals it depends on can change in any release, so the main risk is drift.
